DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
The paper recommends ParcelLine for the standard parcel contract from October, on three grounds:
- it is cheapest on our 70/30 weight mix;
- all three carriers met the service requirements in the trial;
- ParcelLine's tracking app cut "where is my order?" contacts.

The price arithmetic is correct, and the randomised trial is good evidence. But the paper's own Table 1 shows ParcelLine **failing two of our four stated requirements**. Once damage and loss costs are included, ParcelLine becomes the **most expensive** option, not the cheapest.

## 1. ParcelLine fails two requirements

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time delivery of at least 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage below 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |

- §3's statement that on-time delivery "was above 95% for all three" is false, and your description repeats it.
- The damage requirement isn't mentioned anywhere after §2, even though the paper itself says damage matters commercially.
- These gaps are well beyond chance on 5,000 parcels each:
  - on-time: 93.1% against 96.2% is a difference of about 7 standard errors;
  - damage: about 45 damaged parcels against about 20 for SwiftDrop is a difference of about 3 standard errors.

## 2. With damage and loss included, ParcelLine costs the most

The paper puts each damaged or lost parcel at £48 but never applies the figure. Here it is applied at 42,000 parcels a month:

| | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery cost (§4, correct) | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damaged and lost parcels a month | 181 | 412 | 134 |
| Damage and loss cost at £48 | £8,670 | £19,760 | £6,450 |
| "Where is my order?" contacts at £3.20 | £1,480 | £810 | £1,340 |
| **Total a month** | **£159,250** | **£166,730** | **£160,250** |

- ParcelLine costs about **£7,500 a month (around £90,000 a year) more than SwiftDrop**, and about £6,500 a month more than Meridian.
- This includes giving ParcelLine full credit for its lower contact rate.
- The £48 figure partly includes customer service time, so there is a small overlap with the contacts line. It doesn't change the order of the three carriers.
- The damage cost doesn't include the one-star reviews the paper links to damaged items, so it, if anything, understates ParcelLine's cost.
- The "save up to £76,000 a year" claim compares delivery prices only. On total cost, the choice would *lose* roughly that much.

## 3. The contact saving can't be credited to the tracking app

- §5 notes that **from 1 May, ParcelLine parcels alone carried the new delivery-day text message.** That is half the trial, applied to one carrier only.
- The lower contact rate can't be separated from the text. Treated this way, the contacts measure isn't a fair comparison, even though the random allocation was fair.
- ParcelLine's later and more often lost parcels would normally *increase* contacts, which suggests the text message did much of the work.
- The text is being rolled out to every carrier, so whatever advantage it gave ParcelLine will disappear.

## 4. Further points

- **Lost-parcel rates rest on very small counts.** At about 5,000 parcels per carrier, 8, 3 and 2 per 10,000 means roughly 4, 1–2 and 1 parcels. Treat those differences as unreliable. The damage and on-time differences are solid.
- **The trial didn't cover peak season.** It ran in April and May. The contract would run from October, through peak trading. SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for similar retailers. ParcelLine's references are mainly lighter fashion parcels, while 30% of our parcels are lamps, mirrors and small furniture. It's worth checking whether ParcelLine's damage was concentrated in the 2–10 kg band.
- **Contract term.** The 12-month term is a fair advantage, but SwiftDrop offers it too.

## 5. What holds up

- **The trial design:** random allocation of about 5,000 parcels per carrier is good, fair evidence on on-time delivery and damage.
- **The price arithmetic:** the weighted costs (£3.55, £3.48, £3.63) and the monthly totals are all correct.
- **The like-for-like features:** all three carriers offer the same collection time, integration, delivery-preference options and photographic proof of delivery.

## 6. What is settled and what is open

**Settled by the paper's own figures:**
- ParcelLine fails the on-time and damage requirements;
- including damage and loss, ParcelLine has the highest total cost;
- the contact advantage is confounded by the text-message trial.

**Open, and what would settle each question:**

| Question | What would settle it |
|---|---|
| SwiftDrop or Meridian | Whether Meridian's slightly better service is worth about £12,000 a year more and a 24-month commitment |
| Peak-season performance | References and data from each carrier's last peak season |
| Where ParcelLine's damage occurs | Damage by weight band from the trial data |
| Each carrier's true contact rate | Contact rates for April only, before the text started, or after the text reaches all carriers |

## 7. Suggested revision to the recommendation

> In a randomised two-month trial, SwiftDrop and Meridian met all our requirements; ParcelLine did not, with on-time delivery of 93.1% and damage of 0.9%. Including damage and loss at £48 a parcel, SwiftDrop has the lowest total cost (about £159,000 a month), followed by Meridian (about £160,000) and ParcelLine (about £167,000). We recommend awarding the contract to SwiftDrop for 12 months from 1 October 2026, subject to peak-season references. Meridian is a close alternative if its higher service levels justify a 24-month term.

I can set out the total-cost table with sensitivity to the £48 figure, if that would help.
